page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.metal is a general-purpose, bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 8259CL processors. It features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps with EBS optimization.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core performance and PassMark CPU scores ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also highly rated, showing strong read and write speeds for large uncached blocks. Real-world application tests show strong performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance is average, and LLM text generation speeds are poor, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

The bare-metal architecture of the m5dn.metal provides qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive applications by eliminating hypervisor overhead. The combination of high-speed local NVMe storage, 100 Gbps networking, and balanced CPU-to-memory allocation makes this server highly suitable for high-throughput databases, caching layers, static web serving, and parallel software compilation tasks.
